title: HCMC-TrafficSnap: A City-Scale Multi-Camera Image Time-Series and Directed Spatial Graph Dataset for Heterogeneous Urban Traffic
description:
HCMC-TrafficSnap is an open-access, city-scale multimodal dataset comprising over 1,000,000 discrete surveillance camera snapshots (~1.22 million frames) coupled with an OpenStreetMap-derived directed road routing distance graph across 608 active traffic surveillance stations in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The dataset spans 7 continuous calendar days (168 consecutive hours) at a 5-minute sampling interval, capturing the visual and spatial dynamics of motorcycle-dominant mixed urban mobility (70-80% two-wheelers).

Key Highlights:

  • Scale: 608 active municipal camera stations (indexed in range [1, 657]) across expressways, arterials, and roundabouts.
  • Temporal Span: 7 continuous days (Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 ICT) at ~300 s polling interval.
  • Visual Modality: 512x288 pixel JPEG snapshots named by {station_id}_{unix_timestamp}.jpg with an average file size of 65.87 KB.
  • Spatial Topology: Directed 608x608 shortest-path routing distance matrix (2,420 valid corridors <= 5.0 km) derived from OpenStreetMap, exhibiting pronounced directional asymmetry (1,054 one-way pairs and 232 distance-asymmetric pairs).
  • Privacy by Design: High pole mounting (>6 m) and sub-Nyquist ground sampling distance physically guarantee zero resolvable faces or license plates (0.00% PII).
  • Applications: Multi-camera self-supervised representation learning, background-foreground scene decomposition, unsupervised incident detection, and spatio-temporal graph neural networks.
